newsitem.title: GERMANY: Management jobs on the line in Daimler revamp.
newsitem.headline: Management jobs on the line in Daimler revamp.

text.p: A sweeping restructuring at Daimler-Benz AG designed to cut costs and boost efficiency could result in mangement job cuts, company sources said on Friday.

According to sources, several hundred jobs at Daimler's headquarters locations around the world will be cut and that the reorganisation will ultimately effect about half of the 3,000 people who work at the offices.
Daimler chairman Juergen Schrempp met around 1,400 executives here on Friday to explain the company's reorganisation plans which were approved by Daimler's supervisory board on Thursday.
"There will be something to change at every work station," a Daimler manager said.

Under the reorganistion plan, Daimler's Mercedes-Benz AG unit will be legally wound down and merged into the group's management structure. The other two major units, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) and Debis AG, will stay fully independent.
Daimler plans to grow in all of its areas of activity and that sales will increase across the board over the next ten years, the group said in its current in-house publication for employees.
Schremmp said that the new group stucture was the basis for this growth and called for the support of Daimler employees to make the restructuring a success.
"We are looking for your support to ensure that what realise plans we have only seen on paper so far," Schrempp said in the newsletter.

Separately, in an interview with the German daily Handelsblatt, Daimler chief financial officer Manfred Gentz said Daimler sales are likely to climb to around 130 billion marks by the year 2000 from near 106 billion marks now.
Gentz added that he did not expect to raise more capital this year. "We have no plans for a classic capital increase this year and probably not in 1998."

The Daimler CFO also said that the stronger dollar should help the company's profits. He said that from a theoretical standpoint, an increase in the dollar of 10 pfennigs should boost operating profit by around 800 million marks.
Gentz said that figure, however, was not hard and fast because of the impact of price pressures abroad and foreign exchange hedging.
Over the long term, Gentz said Daimler bases its business projections on a dollar/mark level of 1.40. In morning trade in Frankfurt on Friday, the dollar stood at 1.63 marks.
